title: Updraft Model for Development of Autonomous Soaring Uninhabited Air Vehicles
relevance: Builds an analytical thermal field from NOAA Desert Rock surface-radiation and rawinsonde observations. Three-minute surface observations and balloon profiles determine statistical convective velocity scale w* (m/s) and mixed-layer depth zi (m), which then set thermal size, spacing, vertical velocity, and maximum height; the paper supplies a code listing and check case. The seasonal test matrix spans w*=0.46–5.02 m/s and mean zi=54–3647 m across its paired cases.
limitations: A parameterized model derived from one desert site, not thermal cross-sections measured aloft or an aircraft flight validation. Its height/scale range is atmospheric and much larger than near-ground RC operating volumes; use as a baseline model family, not as a universal profile. The listing is not executed here.
access: Downloaded from NASA NTRS; NASA record marks public distribution and U.S. Government public use permitted.
license: NASA record: Work of the U.S. Government; Public Use Permitted.
read_depth: Full paper text reviewed for data inputs, units, scale-factor distributions, model description, code appendix, and limits of the test matrix; PDF signature and first-page text verified.

title: The Role of Thermals in the Convective Boundary Layer
relevance: NCAR Electra measurements during AMTEX provide direct thermal statistics through the mixed layer. Humidity, rather than temperature, identifies thermals because upper-layer thermal air can be cooler than its environment. Five-minute, 30-km flight legs were filtered at a 5-km cutoff; thermal segments were selected using humidity anomalies. The analysis finds height-dependent thermal length/count scaling and shows pressure/edge effects and divergence of vertical-velocity variance matter to mean-updraft balance.
limitations: Oceanic cold-air-outbreak campaign and statistical composites, not isolated thermal maps or a low-altitude RC dataset. The publisher PDF endpoint redirected to the article page during this retrieval; no local copy was saved. Numeric comparisons need the full paper, not its abstract alone.
access: Publisher metadata and abstract accessible; publisher PDF request returned the article page rather than a PDF. Not downloaded.
license: Publisher terms apply; redistribution not inferred.
read_depth: Publisher abstract and indexed article text reviewed for measurement campaign, thermal classification, scales, and stated balance terms; no local PDF audit.

It is a useful independent measured-structure reference alongside the earlier AMTEX work.

title: Experimentelle Bestimmung des Verlaufes der Luftfeuchtigkeit in der konvektiven Grenzschicht der Atmosphäre
relevance: DLR integrated a fast miniaturized chilled-mirror hygrometer (up to 10 Hz) into its Discus-2c research sailplane. The abstract reports 26 thermal cross-sections on three summer-2022 days, at different heights and both along and across wind, assessing width, vertical velocity, and temperature/humidity excess relative to ambient air.

title: Measurements from the University of Colorado RAAVEN Uncrewed Aircraft System during ATOMIC
relevance: Documents 39 flights and more than 77 h of observations by a fixed-wing, RC-derived RAAVEN platform near Barbados in Jan–Feb 2020, sampling from about 20 m to 1 km above sea level. The instrument package measures thermodynamic and kinematic state; flight patterns include vertical profiles and multi-kilometre horizontal legs. The public NOAA archive is 39 NetCDF files totaling 703 MB (dataset DOI 10.25921/jhnd-8e58).
limitations: Tropical marine trade-wind boundary layer, not isolated soaring thermals; sampling and platform-derived air-motion estimates must be separated from direct sensor channels. The full 703 MB archive was not downloaded; one selected flight file is indexed separately.
access: Open-access article downloaded. Quality-controlled NetCDF files are publicly available from NOAA NCEI; one complete B1 flight file was downloaded separately from the public listing.

title: ATOMIC CU-RAAVEN UAS: Flight file ATOMIC_CU-RAAVEN_20200127_134726_B1.nc
relevance: One public B1 flight file selected from the 39-file, 703 MB NCEI archive (accession 0225373, DOI 10.25921/jhnd-8e58). Its classic NetCDF has 84,480 records on `time_10hz` and stores aircraft altitude/position/attitude, temperature, relative humidity, pressure, eastward/northward/vertical wind, true airspeed, flight-state and quality flags. Variable metadata gives temperature in K, RH in %, pressure in hPa, wind/TAS in m/s, and direction in degrees. The file's own Creation_Date attribute is 09-Apr-2021; its exact path and checksum are recorded here.
limitations: Single Barbados marine-boundary-layer flight on 2020-01-27; not thermal-core truth or representative of land-based RC-field convection. The 84,480 records are not asserted to be airborne or valid; retain flight and quality flags. Wind components are an aircraft-derived wind product, not independent point anemometers. Basic array inspection found 61,082 finite entries in each wind component and 23,398 nonfinite entries; finiteness does not establish flight or QC validity. No wind retrieval or QC algorithm was recomputed. NCEI's accession landing page lists versions 1.1 and 2.2, but the mapping from this unversioned directory file to a version was not established.
access: Downloaded directly from NOAA NCEI's public HTTPS file listing without authentication; accession metadata lists no legal constraints.
license: NCEI accession metadata lists no legal constraints; no separate reuse license inferred.
read_depth: NetCDF classic CDF-1 signature and SHA-256 verified; opened read-only with SciPy to inspect global attributes, dimensions, variable names, units/descriptions, and sample count. title: Data collected using small uncrewed aircraft systems during the TRacking Aerosol Convection interactions ExpeRiment (TRACER)
relevance: Describes 2022 TRACER field data from fixed-wing RAAVEN and 0.5-m, 2.3-kg CopterSonde platforms near Houston: 131 and 549 flights respectively, with over 200 h combined and profiles/level legs between roughly 20 and 609 m AGL. Measurements sample sea-breeze events, periods before/near convection, and quiescent conditions, providing real small-UAS wind and thermodynamic variability across scales closer to RC operations than a large research glider.
limitations: Campaign data concern heterogeneous coastal boundary-layer evolution, not isolated thermal-core structure. ARM data access requires a free user account; no raw dataset was downloaded. Some reported wind/air-motion variables are retrieved from aircraft/sensor fusion and should not be treated as independent anemometer truth.
access: Open-access paper downloaded. Campaign NetCDF files are served by the ARM Data Center and require a free account.
license: CC BY 4.0.

title: From Flight Logs to Atmospheric Science: Paragliders as Convection Sensors for Identifying Thermal Predictors
relevance: Analyzes 110,730 French paragliding flights from 2017–2024 and 1.47 million detected climb segments. Flight logs provide approximately 1 Hz GNSS position/altitude (barometric altitude when available); the paper reports climbing-rate strength proxies around 1.0 m/s on plains and 1.3 m/s in high mountains, with 1.0–1.5 m/s climb-rate variability. It relates log-derived ceiling/strength/variability to hourly 0.25° ERA5 predictors.
limitations: 2026 arXiv preprint, not peer-reviewed at retrieval. Climb rate is aircraft performance plus air motion, not a direct vertical-wind measurement; correction requires paraglider sink performance. ERA5 predictors are gridded reanalysis, not local observed wind. The article does not provide a standalone public raw-log archive; results are event- and pilot-selection biased.
access: Downloaded from arXiv; v2 dated 2026-09-07.
license: No reuse license stated in the inspected PDF; redistribution not inferred.

title: A Technique for Simulating Turbulence for Aerospace Vehicle Flight Simulation Studies
relevance: Engineering method: parameterizes Dryden spectra by component standard deviations and integral scales, uses nondimensional frequency Ω=ωL/V, and factors the spectra into recursive time-domain filters. This is the clean primary reference for what a Dryden filter assumes and how true airspeed maps spatial scales into time.
limitations: A flight-simulation model, not a field measurement or RC calibration. The report discusses Shuttle-entry simulation; σ and L must come from a separate atmospheric condition and should not be copied as RC defaults.
access: Public NASA NTRS PDF downloaded and checked. This report was already cited in docs/research/wind-physics-primary-sources.md; this is the first local copy in the gusts collection.
license: U.S. Government work; NTRS states public use permitted.
read_depth: Full 22-page PDF text checked, including abstract, nondimensional spectral definitions, filter factorization and variable-parameter discussion.

title: Analysis of Low Altitude Atmospheric Turbulence Data Measured in Flight
relevance: Primary measured evidence: a Beech D-18 recorded all three turbulence components simultaneously at both wingtips while flying 30.5–61 m (100–200 ft) over water in wind-driven turbulence. The report finds vertical-gust probability distributions distinctly non-Gaussian; Dryden fits the inertial-subrange spectra better at some points and von Kármán at others, with low-frequency peaks/dips.
limitations: Full-size aircraft and one over-water campaign; not hobby-aircraft measurements. Its two-wingtip separation is much larger than RC span, and the report does not justify transferring its intensity or scales to other sites.
access: Public NASA NTRS report downloaded and searchable. The report had already been cited in docs/research/wind-physics-primary-sources.md; this is a first local original copy.

title: Analyses and Assessments of Spanwise Gust Gradient Data from NASA B-57B Aircraft
relevance: Instrumented B-57B measurements put gust probes at the nose and both wing tips, enabling simultaneous component statistics and left/right spatial differences. For the report’s main flight analysis, the authors report von Kármán spectra fitting the measured range (0.04–20 Hz) and analyze two-point spectra/correlations; they warn that finite records, aliasing and estimator bias matter.
limitations: Large research aircraft, not RC. The study focuses on a small number of research flights and its conclusions emphasize sensitivity to spatially varying mean trends and signal processing; do not convert its B-57 spanwise statistics directly to a small wing.
access: Public NASA NTRS report downloaded and checked. This report was already cited in docs/research/wind-physics-primary-sources.md; this is its first local copy in the gusts collection.

title: Coherence of Turbulent Wind Under Neutral Wind Conditions at FINO1
relevance: Uses measured winds at three FINO1 mast heights to estimate vertical coherence and compare model predictions. The authors report large differences between measurements and recommended coherence parameters; the Mann-model trend is closer to observations than the standard Kaimal-spectrum/coherence combination in this selected dataset.
limitations: Only January 2008 neutral-stability records were analyzed; it is vertical mast coherence, not spanwise coherence across a small wing or near-surface RC-site data. The paper is in an offshore engineering context.

title: Development of an Unmanned Aerial Vehicle for the Measurement of Turbulence in the Atmospheric Boundary Layer
relevance: Demonstrates two BLUECAT5 fixed-wing UAVs measuring three lower-ABL flights through a stable-to-convective transition. Wind is reconstructed from five-hole pressure-probe data plus inertial/navigation measurements and compared with a 7.62 m sonic tower reference; a 60 Hz probe frequency response corresponds to roughly 0.28 m at the stated cruise speed.
limitations: The aircraft does not directly measure atmospheric wind with an onboard sonic; attitude, yaw, probe calibration and airframe effects enter the reconstructed estimate. Only three flights are shown, and the research UAV is not an RC validation campaign.

title: SAMURAI-S: Sonic Anemometer on a MUlti-Rotor drone for Atmospheric turbulence Investigation in a Sling load configuration
relevance: A research-grade sonic anemometer suspended beneath a multirotor directly measures 3D wind while hovering. Ten 10–28 min comparisons at target heights of 30 and 60 m show good along- and cross-wind agreement with tower sonics, but a consistent overestimate of vertical fluctuations that increases with mean wind speed; the authors also compare spectra and integral statistics.
limitations: This is a multirotor hover/sling-load configuration rather than fixed-wing flight or RC. Only ten samples and a limited set of conditions are studied; raw supporting data are available from authors upon reasonable request, not as an open time-series dataset.

title: In situ measurement of dust devil dynamics: Toward a strategy for Mars
relevance: Field measurements near Eloy, Arizona in June 2001 using a vehicle-mounted wind, temperature and pressure package. The wind sensors sampled at 5 Hz about 3.5 m AGL. The selected encounter does not establish a universal dust-devil profile. No raw wind/pressure time series was acquired.

title: Vorticity from Line-of-Sight Lidar Velocity Scans
relevance: Uses T-REX line-of-sight Doppler lidar observations from Owens Valley to reconstruct cross-plane velocity and spanwise vorticity through continuity. Provides terrain-rotor evidence and a reconstruction method assessed with numerical simulations. The illustrated scan takes 90 s with 105 m along-beam and 2-degree elevation resolution.
limitations: Only line-of-sight velocity is directly sensed. Perpendicular velocity and vorticity are reconstructed under assumptions including approximate two-dimensionality/stationarity. A 90-second scan is not an instantaneous metre-scale flow map. The reported reconstruction performance is assessed against model fields, not independent exact vorticity truth. No raw scans were acquired.

relevance: Analyzes 18 Hz three-component sonic observations and Doppler lidar measurements to characterize gust magnitudes, rise/duration scales and spatial coherence in the Perdigão valley. title: The MATERHORN: Unraveling the Intricacies of Mountain Weather
relevance: Primary overview of the MATERHORN field campaigns at Granite Mountain and Dugway Valley, Utah.
